summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Shere Bangla National Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Sri Lanka posted 222/10 (65.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Bangladesh countered with 110/10 (45.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 120 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, A Dananjaya delivered a masterclass for Sri Lanka (20 Runs & 8 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Sri Lanka 45%) and allowing Sri Lanka to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Sri Lanka's bowling unit, bolstered by Taijul Islam (7 Runs & 8 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Sri Lanka won by 215 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Sri Lanka's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, Sri Lanka won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
